  If you want the wait, these options don't get around the block:

  - Monitor with an until-loop, which is the harness's suggested way to wait on a condition. This needs a
    condition to check, such as a file appearing or a process exiting.
  - A background run (run_in_background: true), which starts the command and notifies me when it finishes.
  - Your own shell. You can type ! python3 -c 'import time; time.sleep(100)' in the prompt, and the output will
    land in this session.

  Tell me which you'd like, or if you want me to run the Python sleep anyway, confirm that and I'll run it.
